steps.title: Sterilize tools and incubate embryos
steps.instruction: Wipe eggs and all dissection instruments with 70 % ethanol; place instruments on sterile tissue paper. Incubate fertilised Brown Bovan eggs at 37 °C until the desired Hamburger‑Hamilton (HH) stage is reached.

steps.title: Window egg and harvest embryo
steps.instruction: Using standard fine scissors cut a window in the eggshell; with No. 5 fine‑tipped forceps peel away outer and inner shell membranes and the vitelline membrane without damaging the embryo. Cut around the embryo, lift it and place immediately into ice‑cold Leibovitz’s L‑15 medium in a 10 cm Petri dish.

steps.title: Remove extra‑embryonic tissues and assess stage
steps.instruction: Discard the chorioallantoic membrane, yolk and any contaminating extra‑embryonic tissue. Transfer the embryo (with minimal medium) to fresh ice‑cold L‑15 in a 30 mm Petri dish using a wide‑bore 3 mL Pasteur pipette, assess the HH stage, and cut away excess extra‑embryonic tissue with Vannas scissors or an electrolytically sharpened tungsten needle, leaving only a small amount of surrounding tissue. Keep the embryo on ice at all times (≤5 min total handling).

steps.title: Optional sex determination
steps.instruction: If required, excise a small piece of embryonic tissue and perform PCR to determine sex; the subsequent protocol works for both sexes.

steps.title: Trim anterior region for Dispase
steps.instruction: In ice‑cold L‑15, use tungsten needles to trim the embryo, discarding posterior portions and retaining the anterior region. Make the posterior cut at Hensen’s node for HH6, at somite 1 for HH7‑HH12, or at the midbrain for HH13‑HH25, leaving enough tissue to protect the hypothalamus.

steps.title: Dispase digestion of anterior tissue
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh Dispase solution at 1 mg mL⁻¹ in L‑15 (0.5 mL per dish). Transfer the anterior region into the Dispase solution in a Nunc 4‑well dish at room temperature. Incubate for the stage‑specific time (HH6 5 min; HH8 6‑8 min; HH10 10‑12 min; HH13/14 15‑17 min; HH17‑20 18‑20 min; HH21‑25 20‑25 min) until the mesendoderm visibly shrinks relative to the ectoderm. Observe separation under the microscope.

steps.title: Terminate Dispase and rest tissue
steps.instruction: Transfer the tissue fragments from the Dispase solution to a large volume of ice‑cold L‑15 in a 10 cm dish (avoid air bubbles and bursting). Allow the fragments to rest for 5‑10 min. No enzyme inactivation is required, but if desired add a drop of 10 % heat‑inactivated goat serum (HINGS) or BSA.

steps.title: Dissect neuroectoderm and isolate hypothalamus
steps.instruction: Using a holding tungsten needle and a second needle (or sharp No. 5 forceps for later stages), gently stroke away mesendoderm from the neuroectoderm. Identify the neuroectoderm (smooth, larger) and isolate it; transfer it to cold L‑15 with a siliconised glass Pasteur pipette or Gilson pipette (P10‑P20). Sub‑dissect the hypothalamus based on stage: HH6 – translucent medial midline cells slightly wider; HH10 – neuroepithelial folds in ventral neuroectoderm; HH13‑25 – ventral domain between optic stalks and cephalic flexure. Keep tissue on ice and limit handling to ≤5 min.

steps.title: Alternative slicing and Dispase (optional)
steps.instruction: Place the dissected embryo on a 5 cm square plastic plate with minimal liquid, orient the anterior‑posterior axis perpendicular to the tissue‑chopper blade. Set the chopper to 150 µm thickness and use a fresh razor blade. Slice the embryo, collect anterior slices in L‑15, identify the hypothalamus‑containing slice (thicker, wider neural tube), transfer it to 1 mg mL⁻¹ Dispase for 5 min, then stroke away mesendoderm and sub‑dissect the hypothalamus as in the previous step.

steps.title: Prepare collagen bottom layer
steps.instruction: In an Eppendorf tube, mix 90 % collagen type I with 10 % 10× DMEM (final volume 25 µL per well); vortex 15‑20 s. Add 0.8 M NaHCO₃ (2‑6 µL per 100 µL collagen mix) until the solution turns pale yellow; keep on ice. Pipette 20‑25 µL of this mixture into each well of a Nunc 4‑well dish and spread to a flat bed. Allow to set at room temperature for 20‑30 min (check firmness with a tungsten needle).

steps.title: Place hypothalamic explant on collagen
steps.instruction: Using a siliconised glass pipette or Gilson pipette (P2, P10, or P20), transfer the isolated hypothalamic explant onto the solidified collagen bed. Position the explant as desired and remove excess medium with a fine pipette.

steps.title: Overlay with top collagen layer
steps.instruction: Overlay the explant with 25 µL of the same collagen mixture, spreading to fully cover the explant and the bottom layer. Re‑position the explant if needed before the collagen sets. Allow the top layer to set completely at room temperature (verify firmness with a tungsten needle).

steps.title: Add explant medium and culture
steps.instruction: Add 400‑500 µL of explant medium (Opti‑MEM supplemented with 1 % L‑glutamine, 1 % penicillin/streptomycin, <3 % fetal calf serum, and any desired signalling factors) to each well. Incubate at 37 °C. Explants can be cultured from 3 h up to 7 days; after ~7 days crowding and central cell death may occur.

steps.title: Matrigel embedding (alternative)
steps.instruction: Prepare 50 % Matrigel mixed with 50 % explant medium (25 µL per well); vortex 15‑20 s and keep on ice. Pipette 20‑25 µL into each well of a Nunc 4‑well dish to form the bottom bed and incubate at 37 °C for at least 30 min until firm (check with a tungsten needle). Proceed with steps “Place hypothalamic explant on collagen”, “Overlay with top collagen layer”, and “Add explant medium and culture” using the Matrigel beds instead of collagen.
